title: The Plasma Instance omits the planning, GovOps review and Artifact Edit Proposal records that every other Instance carries
content:
Every other Instance Configuration Document in the Osero Artifact carries a Data Repository with three fixed children — Initial Planning, Operational GovOps Review, and Artifact Edit Proposal — recording how the Invocation was planned, reviewed and written into the Atlas.

The Plasma Instance does not. A.6.1.1.7.2.5.3.2.1.2 (Operational Process Definition) and A.6.1.1.7.2.5.3.2.1.3 (Data Repository) are present as headers with no children beneath them, while the Ecosystem Upkeep, Upkeep Rebate, Executor Accord and Root Edit Instances all populate the full triad.

The deviation is informative in two directions. If the omission is intentional, it means the Pioneer Chain Instance was created through a path that did not generate the standard invocation record. If it is an oversight, it is exactly the kind of gap the uniform skeleton exists to make visible — a reader can spot it precisely because every sibling has the structure.

Either way it shows the limit of structure-as-enforcement. The Artifact's layout makes the missing record obvious to anyone reading, but nothing in the document prevents an Instance from being recorded without its provenance. The uniformity is a convention maintained by drafters, not a constraint imposed on them.
description: Its Operational Process Definition and Data Repository are empty headers, breaking the uniform Instance skeleton used throughout the rest of the Osero Artifact.
